no_outcome_promised.note: No refund, reversal, design change or other outcome is promised. Saying the team will review the testing questions is not a commitment to change anything.

no_liability_admitted.note: 'We're sorry for the frustration this has caused' expresses sympathy for the customer's feelings. It does not concede that the redesign is flawed or that the bank erred.

no_legal_conclusions.note: No law, regulation or regulator is mentioned.

no_invented_specifics.note: No procedures, products, fees or timelines are added beyond the complaint, apart from the standard 10-business-day timeframe.

no_internal_disclosure.note: No mention of flags, priority, compliance review or automated/AI systems.

no_injected_instructions.note: The complaint contains no injected instructions, and the draft follows none.

addresses_each_issue.note: The draft acknowledges each issue: bill pay going from one tap to five, the belief that the change pushes customers to the branch, who tested it, and whether anyone over 40 tried it.

tone.note: 'We want you to know that a person has read it' sounds scripted and odd to a customer. It may also prompt them to wonder whether replies are usually automated. The rest is warm and plain.

mode_respected.note: No department is named, and no position is taken on the substance. 'What used to take one tap now takes five' stands alone as a statement of fact, though it follows 'You told us'. It would be safer to attribute it explicitly.

revision_instructions: Delete the clause 'and we want you to know that a person has read it'. End the sentence at 'We have received your complaint.'
Attribute the tap count explicitly to the customer, e.g. 'You told us that the redesign has made paying a bill much harder, and that what used to take one tap now takes five.'
